status: Official screenshot observation and proposed DSH adaptation; not runtime verification

purpose.en: Replace the rejected promotional landing-page direction with a quiet, usable native conversation client, learning from visible Claude and ChatGPT interface structure.
purpose.zh: 依据 Claude 和 ChatGPT 可见的界面结构，将被否定的宣传落地页方向改为安静、可用的原生对话客户端。

method.retrieval: Public Apple iTunes lookup API, US storefront; downloaded screenshot URLs from seller metadata through Apple's mzstatic CDN. Requested the same image resource with a 1320x2868bb.png rendition suffix for readability. No accounts or application login used.
method.viewing: Actually opened all 17 iPhone promotional screenshots plus the first iPad screenshot of each app with the image-capable Read tool. Evidence below identifies the most relevant images; each download has its own newly created directory under build/references.
method.scope: Observe only the interface visible inside each promotional composition. Outside-device headlines, photographs, gradients, enlarged callouts and device frames are advertising, not application screen layout.
limits: The lookup's current version is the listing version at retrieval; Apple does not tie each screenshot to that exact binary or disclose its capture date.

Static seller-supplied images can be staged, enlarged or cropped. They do not verify gestures, navigation destinations, animation, latency, accessibility, precise point sizes or functional correctness.
No fully opened history drawer appears in the reviewed images. Claude's code-review task list is not evidence of its general conversation-history layout.
The Claude empty-state evidence is an angled promotional photograph with part of the phone obscured. No ChatGPT empty state appears in the reviewed set.
Images predominantly show light appearance. No general dark-mode behavior was established.
No DSH build, simulator run, device run or user study was performed by this reference researcher. Proposed changes below are not implementation claims.

evidence.visible: Left menu glyph; right new-conversation and overflow glyphs; right-aligned neutral user bubble; unboxed assistant text; map result. The map is enlarged outside the application crop by the promotional composition.

Attachment thumbnails and filenames precede a user bubble. Assistant prose is unboxed. A file result shows a title and file type. Rounded bottom composer contains entered text above plus, model, microphone and send controls; send is accented orange.

Task filters All, Blocked, In progress and partial Done; rows with task title, time, icon and context. An enlarged approval card contains task title, project, question and Approve. This image is a staged task-list composition, not a verified navigation flow.

Angled phone photograph shows Claude mark, a single What are you thinking? prompt, and a nearby composer. No stack of feature cards is visible in the unobscured area. Exact placement and hidden controls cannot be established.
Wider conversation presentation with neutral user bubble, assistant prose, map result and bottom composer. Menu and new-conversation/overflow glyphs occupy the top corners; no sidebar is open.

Menu at top left, compose and overflow at top right; right-aligned pale-blue prompts and left-aligned images; bottom pill composer with plus, placeholder, microphone and blue voice control. Pastel gradient is outside the device screen.

Short user prompt in a right bubble; two unboxed left-aligned assistant paragraphs; muted copy, speaker, thumbs, retry and share glyphs directly below response; generous unused canvas; bottom composer.

Image attachment sits above its user prompt. Assistant response uses short bold headings and paragraphs on the plain canvas; no surrounding assistant card. Composer overlays the bottom edge of the long response in the static image.
An email draft has its own subdued bordered surface with type, recipients, subject and body; edit/copy/send glyphs are attached to that object. Surrounding conversation canvas stays plain.

observedPatterns.observed: Inside the app crop, small navigation controls frame a large conversation area. Large promotional headlines belong outside the app crop.
observedPatterns.apply: Use an inline native navigation title and compact toolbar; allocate the main viewport to conversation or a single useful empty state. Remove the giant product slogan and stacked introductory feature cards.

observedPatterns.observed: A menu glyph consistently appears at the left and creation/overflow glyphs at the right. An opened history drawer and its grouping are not visible.
observedPatterns.apply: Provide a clearly labelled history entry and native searchable conversation list, with iPad sidebar/detail. Row structure, search and grouping are DSH proposals, not claims about these apps' hidden drawers.

observedPatterns.observed: The visible Claude empty conversation has one short invitation and a composer, with ample blank space. The source is an angled photo, not a full flat capture.
observedPatterns.apply: Use one short Chinese prompt and at most two actionable text rows. In the current preview expose a clearly labelled local-demo entry and real computer-discovery entry; show an active composer only inside the explicit demo or a future capable remote session.

observedPatterns.observed: A single rounded input surface groups text and adjacent controls. Claude's example has text above a control row; ChatGPT's short composer fits controls on one row.
observedPatterns.apply: Keep one native multiline composer in a keyboard-aware safe-area inset. Use restrained border/fill and one send-or-stop control. Omit attachment, voice and model-picker controls until their actual capability exists; do not copy screenshot model names.

observedPatterns.observed: User text sits in right-aligned tinted bubbles; assistant text is left-aligned and unboxed. No repeated large assistant identity heading is visible in these crops.
observedPatterns.apply: Retain compact pale-blue or neutral user bubbles and unboxed assistant prose. Remove repeated decorative sparkle/brand rows before every answer; preserve accessible role semantics.

observedPatterns.observed: Paragraph spacing and modest headings organize assistant content. ChatGPT uses sans-serif prose; Claude's visible assistant prose is serif, so there is no shared typeface to replicate.
observedPatterns.apply: Choose native system text styles for DSH Chinese content, with readable paragraph spacing and a restrained width on iPad. Treat exact sizes, line lengths and Dynamic Type behavior as implementation choices requiring native verification.

observedPatterns.observed: Muted answer-action glyphs sit immediately after the answer; an email object keeps its own actions inside its header.
observedPatterns.apply: Place the implemented copy action beneath the completed answer in a quiet row; give it a native accessibility label and adequate hit target. Do not add nonfunctional rating, retry, share or read-aloud controls for visual similarity.

observedPatterns.observed: Conversation canvases are mainly white or warm neutral, with subtle input and user-message surfaces. Strong accent appears on selected actions; the surrounding marketing photography and gradients are not the conversation background.
observedPatterns.apply: Use white/near-black native canvases, quiet separators and limited neutral surfaces. Keep documented DeepSeek blue for functional focus, selected state and send controls; avoid decorative gradients, large tinted panels and repeated heavy shadows.

observedPatterns.observed: Distinct containers identify concrete objects such as a file result or email draft, while ordinary assistant paragraphs stay on the canvas.
observedPatterns.apply: Reserve a compact container for a real structured object or pending approval. Present activity as a quiet disclosure row. Do not turn every explanation, navigation link or product benefit into a card.

observedPatterns.observed: The task-list composition places task title, time, project context and pending decision close together; an approval question has its action directly below it.
observedPatterns.apply: Keep an approval attached to its conversation. Show computer, workspace, exact operation and current validity in the detail sheet, with allow-once and reject actions. Use only actual timestamps and status; this source does not establish acknowledgment or execution semantics.

proposedNativeDesign.status: Recommendations for the parent implementation team; not applied by this research task
proposedNativeDesign.direction: An understated conversation tool using native system typography and the project's documented DeepSeek functional accent.
proposedNativeDesign.shell: NavigationSplitView where appropriate: searchable history on iPad; native navigation stack or sheet for history on iPhone. Toolbar contains title, history/back and new-conversation only when available. Computer discovery and settings remain reachable without occupying the transcript.
proposedNativeDesign.firstScreen: Use a quiet DSH title and one short context sentence. Offer Try local conversation and Sign in to discover computers as real actions; no marketing hero, generic sparkle, numbered feature cards or invented capability badges. If a demo is already active, return to its conversation.
proposedNativeDesign.emptyConversation: Single short invitation, optional useful example that fills the draft, then the composer. Keep the page sparse; do not fill unused space with product claims.
proposedNativeDesign.history: Native searchable rows: title first, workspace/computer context second, pending state when real. Local demonstration sessions are visibly local and are never mixed into discovered-host data. Group only from actual dates if grouping is useful.
proposedNativeDesign.transcript: Unboxed assistant prose; compact user bubble; contextual copy action; collapsed reasoning/activity; a small pending-approval entry that opens native details. Preserve reading position and return-to-latest behavior already present in source.
proposedNativeDesign.composer: One rounded multiline field with send/stop, native keyboard handling and at least 44-point interactive targets. No model, microphone or attachment ornament without implemented support. Preserve draft isolation and disabled states.
proposedNativeDesign.modeBoundary: One compact persistent Local demo label, with contextual explanation that replies are preset and commands are not executed. Keep destructive-exit explanations near exits and approval outcome explanations near decisions; remove repetitive decorative demo warnings from every surface.
proposedNativeDesign.discoveryBoundary: Keep signed-in, discovered and secure-session states distinct. An online server-reported host does not enable a remote composer or acquire a connected/verified badge. Retain explicit loading, error, empty and offline states.
proposedNativeDesign.motion: No animation observations can be drawn from these screenshots. Prefer native navigation, sheet and keyboard transitions; let the motion specialist validate interruptibility and Reduce Motion on the actual app.
validationNeeded: Native compact-screen and iPad visual review, including keyboard and long Chinese content.
Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, light/dark contrast, reduced-motion and reduced-transparency checks.
Real service and Host validation before enabling any remote-session operation.

doNotCopy: Promotional photography, illustrations, generated sample media or screenshot pixels
Model names, account states, counts or capabilities shown in examples
reuseBoundary.assetPolicy: Downloaded Apple-hosted images remain local research evidence under build/references. They are not licensed application assets and must not be bundled or copied into DSH branding. No upstream code or assets were copied.

projectContext.sourceBoundary: At review time ChatView source included local-demo labels, per-session composer state, user bubbles, unboxed assistant prose, activity/approval containers and return-to-latest behavior. These are source observations, not runtime verification.
projectContext.designConflictForParent: The existing product-design document still recommends a welcome slogan and extensive preview messaging. Revise the owning bilingual specification to match the user's newly requested quiet chat direction; this researcher changed neither docs nor Swift source.
